verses.1: Let your hearts not be troubled. You believe in God; believe also in me.
verses.2: In my Father’s house there are many rooms. If it were not so, I would have told you, for I am going to prepare a place for you.
verses.3: And if I go and prepare a place for you, I will come again and take you to myself, so that where I am you may be also.
verses.4: You know the way to the place where I am going.
verses.5: Thomas said to him, “Lord, we do not know where you are going. How can we know the way?”
verses.6: Jesus said to him, “I am the way, and the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me.
verses.7: If you had known me, you would have known my Father also. From now on, you know him and have seen him.”
verses.8: Philip said to him, “Lord, show us the Father, and it is enough for us.”
verses.9: Jesus said to him, “Have I been with you for so long, and yet you do not know me, Philip? Whoever has seen me has seen the Father. How can you say, ‘Show us the Father’?”
verses.10: Do you not believe that I am in the Father and the Father is in me? The words I say to you I do not speak on my own, but the Father who dwells in me does his works.
verses.11: Believe me that I am in the Father and the Father is in me. Or believe because of the works themselves.
verses.12: Amen, amen, I say to you, whoever believes in me will do the works I do, and they will do greater works than these, because I am going to the Father.
verses.13: And whatever you ask in my name, this I will do, so that the Father may be glorified in the Son.
verses.14: If you ask me anything in my name, I will do it.
verses.15: If you love me, you will keep my commandments.
verses.16: And I will ask the Father, and he will give you another Helper, to be with you forever,
verses.17: the Spirit of truth, whom the world cannot receive, because it neither sees him nor knows him. You know him, for he dwells with you and will be in you.
verses.18: I will not leave you as orphans; I am coming to you.
verses.19: A little while longer and the world will see me no more, but you will see me, because I live and you will live.
verses.20: On that day you will know that I am in the Father and you are in me and I am in you.
verses.21: The one who keeps my commandments and obeys them is the one who loves me. And the one who loves me will be loved by my Father, and I will love them and reveal myself to them.
verses.22: Judas (not Iscariot) said to him, “Lord, what has happened that you are going to reveal yourself to us and not to the world?”
verses.23: Jesus answered him, “If anyone loves me, they will keep my word, and my Father will love them, and we will come to them and make our home with them.
verses.24: The one who does not love me does not keep my words. The word that you hear is not mine but the Father’s who sent me.
verses.25: These things I have spoken to you while I am still with you.
verses.26: But the Helper, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, will teach you all things and will remind you of everything I have told you.
verses.27: Peace I leave with you; my peace I give to you. Not as the world gives do I give to you. Let your hearts not be troubled, nor let them be afraid.
verses.28: You heard me say, ‘I am going away, and I will come to you.’ If you loved me, you would rejoice that I am going to the Father, for the Father is greater than I.
verses.29: And I have told you this now, before it happens, so that when it happens you may believe.
verses.30: I will not speak with you much longer, for the ruler of this world is coming, and he has no power over me.
verses.31: But I say this, so that you may know that I love the Father, and just as the Father has commanded me, so I do. Rise, let us go from here.

notes:
Notes
- v. 10: "The words I say to you I do not speak on my own" — the phrase "ἀπʼ ἐμαυτοῦ" is translated as "on my own" rather than the more literal "from myself."
- v. 28: "the Father is greater than I" — the original says "ὁ πατὴρ μείζων μού ἐστιν," which is translated as "the Father is greater than I" without adding "in being" or other theological qualifiers.
- v. 22: "Judas (not Iscariot)" — the Greek explicitly distinguishes between Judas the Iscariot and this other Judas by name, so the parenthetical clarification is added for clarity.
